upstream.scope: Named saved views in a server-side, per-user, versioned settings file (D1 §§6.3, 7.3, 26-27; D2 T32): a view holds columns, sort, command and user filters, table/tree and thread controls, and nothing about a process, selection, action intent or confirmation, endpoint, credential, geometry or appearance; a button-based switcher from standard widgets; bounded, checksummed, atomic writes with one backup and version migration; no protocol, registry, SDK, runtime, client or dependency change

entries.feature: A saved view holds exactly the column layout, sort, committed command filter, user filter (all, mine or the user field's text), tree mode and thread settings; the settings hold 1-8 uniquely named views scoped to the process source and the active view; the format is versioned UTF-8 text with escaped values and an FNV-1a checksum line; a newer version is refused from its first line and never interpreted, version 1 is migrated, and every bound (64 KiB, 256 lines, 8 views, 64-byte names, filter and user-field bounds) refuses the whole file; unknown catalogue keys are dropped with a note while unknown structure refuses the file; every truncation and single-byte damage is refused without panic
entries.scope: PX-069/settings (src/settings.rs) SavedView, Settings, parse, encode, declared_version; src/settings.rs unit tests; tests/saved_views_test.rs bounds_are_enforced_on_every_read_and_every_change, a_version_1_file_is_migrated_and_written_back_as_the_current_version

entries.feature: The settings store reads only a regular file, checks its size before opening it and reads at most the bound plus one byte; a damaged file falls back to a valid same-source backup and never replaces it; a newer version, another application's or source's file, an unreadable file or a non-file makes the store read-only and is never overwritten; a save copies the valid current file to settings.bak and writes the new file through a create_new 0600 temporary file, sync_all, rename and a directory flush, so a crash at any step leaves the file whole, old or new; stale temporaries are swept
entries.scope: PX-069/settings_file (src/settings_file.rs) SettingsStore::load, save, default_path_from; tests/saved_views_test.rs truncated, oversized, newer-version, foreign/other-source/non-file, interrupted-save and atomic-rename tests; Linux rust:1-bookworm run

entries.feature: A switcher row of standard Buttons (one per view slot, the active one labelled, empty slots disabled and collapsed), a View name TextInput and Save as new view, Rename active view, Delete active view and Restore default views, created only with a settings store and disabled while it is read-only; a slot applies the view the server holds through the process list's own setters, so rows keep their ItemIds; Rename and Delete never reach the process view or the action gate, so no identity, selection or pending intent changes and nothing is executed; deleting the active view applies none; a restarted srtop applies the active view before serving clients

entries.feature: --settings-path PATH and --no-settings choose the settings file (mutually exclusive, once each, a path needs a process source); the live source defaults to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/srtop/settings or the platform configuration directory, while fixture sources keep none unless a path is named; every existing test that starts the live source passes --no-settings, so no test reads or writes the real user's settings

entries.feature: The PX-008 audit admits file writes in src/settings_file.rs alone (OpenOptions, OpenOptionsExt, DirBuilder, DirBuilderExt, fs::rename, fs::remove_file, .write and .write_all), pinned to exactly one OpenOptions::new() and one create_new with no truncate, append or .create(true); the same writer in any other file and every other rule in the settings module stay refused; the saved views' node constants are admitted with ACTIVATE and the name field with TEXT_EDIT only, and no intent, confirmation, PID or process identity appears in the settings file
